# dsh-java-mcp
English | 中文

A DeepSeek Harness **bundle** that wires the JavaLens
MCP server into DSH automatically. JavaLens is

built on Eclipse JDT; after
installation its tools are available to the model as native DSH tools u

nder the
`mcp__javalens__*` namespace — including symbol search, find references, type
hierarchy, di

agnostics, call hierarchy, change impact analysis, data/control
flow and refactorings (returned as t

call hierarchy, change impact analysis, data/control
flow and refactorings (returned as text edits).
## Why?

`grep "save("` returns 47 hits, including `saveButton`, comments and same-named
methods of unrelated

classes. JDT-based analysis returns exactly the 12 real
calls of `UserService.save()` because it re

solves types, inheritance and
overloads. This plugin implements the idea from the original discussio

n: give
the LLM a Java MCP server so code analysis becomes compiler-accurate instead of
textual.
## How?

There is no special syntax: install and enable the bundle, then describe the
outcome you want in nat

ural language. JavaLens starts without a project in each
session; the model loads the workspace once

(`load_project`) and then works
through the 75 tools. Four proven starting points:
### 1. Fix the diagnostics in one go

> "Load the Java project in this workspace with JavaLens, then fix every
> fixable diagnostic: use `

diagnose_and_fix`, apply the returned text edits to
> the source files, and re-run `get_diagnostics`
until it is clean."

The model runs `get_diagnostics`, `diagnose_and_fix` (or `get_quick_fixes` plus
`apply_quick_fix`) a

nd applies the edits with its file-editing tool. JavaLens
never writes files itself, so every change
stays visible and reviewable.
### 2. Remove dead code

> "Find unused methods and fields with `find_unused_code`, remove the ones that
> are clearly dead,
and list what you deleted and where."
### 3. Rename safely across the project

> "Rename `Service.describeAll` to `summarizeAll` using `rename_symbol`, apply
> the edits in all af

fected files, and verify with `get_diagnostics` that
> nothing broke."

The rename returns one edit per occurrence — declaration plus every call site —
so the model can app
ly them all in one step.
### 4. Check the blast radius before changing code

> "I want to change the signature of `Service.describeAll`. Before touching
> anything, use `analyze

_change_impact` and the call hierarchy to list every
> affected file and call site, then summarize t

he risk. If the project has
> tests, also name the tests that would need to run."

This is where JDT beats `grep`: the analysis follows overrides, interface calls
and transitive calle
rs instead of matching text.
## Requirements
| Requirement | Details |

| DSH | Desktop or CLI **0.2.x**; documented and tested with 0.2.1-rc.3. |
| Node.js | a Node.js ins
tallation providing **`npx` on PATH**. The Desktop app bundles Node 24.21 and pnpm, but **no npm/npx
**; on a Desktop-only machine either install Node.js LTS or switch the launcher to `pnpm dlx` (see L

auncher alternatives). |
| Java | **21 or newer** (`java -version`), JavaLens runtime; it must be re

achable for the DSH process via `PATH` or `JAVA_HOME` |
| Network | only the first start downloads `

javalens-mcp` (~38 MB) through `npx`; afterwards it comes from the npx cache |
| OS | Windows, macOS

mcp` (~38 MB) through `npx`; afterwards it comes from the npx cache |
| OS | Windows, macOS, Linux |
## Installation

The Desktop profile is **owned by the app**: `dsh plugin --profile desktop …`
is rejected with `prof

ile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron
application`. The Desktop app also uses its own

DSH home
(`%APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness`), which a separate CLI installation cannot
reach.
### Desktop app (recommended)

1. Open the **Plugins** page in the sidebar.
2. In the install field, enter a **GitHub address or a

*Plugins** page in the sidebar.
2. In the install field, enter a **GitHub address or a local path**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

(or the URL `https://github.com/weymann/dsh-java-mcp`). For a local
checkout, enter the absolute pat

h `C:\Projects\dsh-java-mcp`.
3. Install. DSH recognises the bundle through `dsh.bundle` in `package

.json`
and adds it to the profile as a dependency; the Plugins page shows it as
installed but **not

yet enabled** — installing alone does not add it to
`dsh.profile.bundles`.
4. Click **Enable now** i

n the install dialog (or switch the bundle on its
card). Only then is it appended to `dsh.profile.bu

ndles`, and its
`cordis.patch.yml` is applied as a patch layer — no manual YAML editing.
5. If the `

mcp__javalens__*` tools do not appear in the chat immediately,
restart the app.

Then ask in the chat, for example: "list all methods in `demo.Foo`" — the model
will call the JavaLe

in the chat, for example: "list all methods in `demo.Foo`" — the model
will call the JavaLens tools.

> The GitHub variant requires the repository to be pushed and reachable from
> your machine via `git

`. A local path always works and is the fastest way to
> try the plugin.
### CLI (own profiles: web, headless)

The `dsh` CLI only manages its own profiles, not the Desktop profile. Choose a
CLI version that matc

hes your DSH version (`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.3` is
published on npm):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

After DSH starts, load the Java project once per session through the model:
`mcp__javalens__load_pro

ject` with the absolute workspace path. The model sees
the workspace path in its session context, so

a prompt like "load the Java
project in this workspace and list unused methods" is enough.
### Local development / installing from the checkout

- **Desktop:** Plugins page, install the absolute path to the checkout.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

This plugin is a pure configuration bundle: `index.js` is an empty ESM module
(the same convention a

s the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` bundles), and DSH's
official MCP client does the work. There is

no network access beyond the
initial `npx` download; project code and analysis results stay local.
